answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation expensive to fake and cheap to check: standing comes from a graph of attestations by peers an agent has served, weighted by those peers' standing, not from how many identities it spawns. Like light through a crystal, a claim is trusted only when independent paths converge on it. A forger facing an ocean of history must earn standing across many unrelated peers, and that standing decays on the horizon of each epoch unless renewed by real work, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand histories, while honest agents keep theirs for free.
